subject: open-codex
title: Fork delta is exactly the transport swap Responses-API -> Chat-Completions plus a five-provider key/baseURL/model table; loop and sandbox byte-heritage upstream
one_why: Clean example of what a 'make it run on anything' fork minimally touches: chat-vs-responses item normalization (function.name vs name, call_id vs id) and an env-var-keyed provider fallback ladder (config.ts:40-48) - and notably zero tests for the four added providers (tests/config.test.tsx:64-77 covers openai only).

subject: open-codex
title: Esc-esc cancellation defended by generation counter, dual stream/exec abort controllers, and synthetic tool outputs replayed for unresolved call_ids so the next request satisfies the API contract
one_why: The 'No tool output found for function call' 400 after a mid-tool cancel is a contract problem every streaming tool-calling loop inherits; keeping call_ids in pendingAborts and emitting {output:'aborted'} tool messages on the next run is the minimal repair, and the FakeStream-yields-before-cancel test pins the exact race window.

subject: open-codex
title: FakeOpenAI vi.mock + hand-built FakeStream assert loop semantics (cancel, terminate, rate-limit backoff, max-tokens, retry) across 14 agent-*.test.ts files
one_why: With only ~5k test LOC the corpus still proves error-taxonomy behavior (which error yields which user-visible message and whether the loop returns or rethrows) instead of asserting existence - cheap pattern that transfers to any provider-SDK loop.

subject: open-codex
title: SandboxType.LINUX_LANDLOCK declared in the enum but never implemented; full-auto on Linux silently runs the same rawExec path as no-sandbox
evidence: codex-cli/src/utils/agent/sandbox/interface.ts:5; codex-cli/src/utils/agent/exec.ts:40 (seatbelt-or-rawExec ternary); no landlock code anywhere in src/
one_why: The CLI help promises '--full-auto automatically run commands in a sandbox' (cli.tsx:74-77) while Linux gets zero kernel enforcement with no runtime warning; milder than the claurst rung because README:151 honestly states 'Linux - there is no sandboxing by default', but the runtime silently degrades on the dominant server platform - caps safety-enforcement at 4.

subject: open-codex
title: Always-approve cache keys collapse 'bash -lc <script>' to the script's first word, so one 'always approve' on git status mutes prompting for every git invocation for the session
one_why: 'Always approve this command' silently becomes 'always approve this program' - git push --force inherits consent from git status; the key abstraction discards exactly the arguments that distinguish safe from destructive invocations, and approvals.test.ts does not pin the granularity.

subject: open-codex
title: Zero compaction: full history replayed every request, no usage accounting, overflow is one terminal message telling the user to run /clear
one_why: Token-economy at the codel-1 rung: the only budget code in the repo is the legacy singlepass zip size-map (src/utils/singlepass/context_limit.ts:17-40); historical note - the TS codex line never grew compaction, which is part of why the Rust rewrite replaced it.

subject: open-codex
title: Pre-AGENTS.md project-doc convention preserved: codex.md/.codex.md/CODEX.md discovered from .git-rooted cwd, 32 kB cap with truncation warning
one_why: Snapshot of the memory-file lineage one generation before AGENTS.md standardization; the byte-capped-truncate-with-warning handling of oversized project docs is a detail still worth having.

subject: open-codex
title: Earliest codex rollout format: per-conversation JSON auto-saved on every message change with view-only 'codex -v' replay - persistence without resume
evidence: codex-cli/src/components/chat/terminal-chat.tsx:112 (saveRollout); codex-cli/src/cli.tsx:233-245 (-v parse + JSON.parse as AppRollout); codex-cli/src/app.tsx:14
one_why: Ancestor of the codex-rs rollout JSONL journal: same save-and-inspect idea, one full rewrite away from resume/fork - useful for dating which journal capabilities existed in the TS era.

subject: open-codex
title: Preserves the abandoned --full-context mode: whole repo flattened into one prompt using per-path cumulative size maps to budget directory-level truncation
one_why: Removed upstream and absent from every other subject in this corpus; the bottom-up size map (every path's subtree byte total) driving what to keep when the repo exceeds the window is a genuinely different answer to context assembly than agent-loop exploration.
